learning_outcomes.text: Analyze the stresses in load carrying members subject to direct axial or shear force.
Determine the displacement of the long members subject to axial load.
Calculate the stresses and angle of twist in the shafts subject to torque.
Calculate the bending stresses in the beams.
Calculate the shear stresses in the beams subject to transverse shear force.
Analyze the stress state of the members subject to combined load.
Understand the concept of principal stresses and max in-plane shear stress by using the stress transformation equations and Mohr's circle.
Calculate the stresses for the elastic bodies.
Calculate the strain and deformation for the elastic bodies.
Calculate the stress state at a point under the combined loading effect for the mechanical design.
Understand the principle stress concept and ability to apply the stress transformation.

syllabus_topics: STRESS: equilibrium of a deformable body, average normal and shear stress, bearing stress.
STRESS: allowable stress, factor of safety STRAIN: deformation.
STRAIN: normal and shear strain, MECHANICAL PROPERTIES OF MATERIALS: the tension test, Hooke's law, Poisson's ratio.
AXIAL LOAD: elastic deformation of an axially loaded members, principle of superposition.
AXIAL LOAD: statically indeterminate axially loaded member, thermal stress.
TORSION: the torsion formula, power transmission, statically indeterminate torque-loaded members.
Midterm Exam I: BENDING: The flexure formula.
TRANSVERSE SHEAR: the shear formula, shear stresses in beams, shear flow in built-up members.
COMBINED LOADING: state of stress caused by combined loading.
COMBINED LOADING: state of stress caused by combined loading
Midterm Exam I: COMBINED LOADING: state of stress caused by combined loading.
STRESS TRANSFORMATION: plane stress transformation, general equations of plane stress transformation
bibliography: Mechanics of Materials, F. P.Beer and E. R. Johnston, Mc-Graw Hill Comp., England
Mechanics of Materials, R. C. Hibbeler, Prentice-Hall Inc., USA
